text:
liam: hey all, second day troubleshooting my dev bootstrap on an M2 Mac. ran the onboarding script but node builds fail when compiling native modules, and my asdf nodejs install keeps hitting "npm: command not found" after install. i also use chezmoi-managed dotfiles so not sure where to tweak shell rc. any pointers?

jess: welcome liam! common Apple Silicon stuff: make sure Homebrew is the arm64 install (`/opt/homebrew`). `brew install openssl@3 pkg-config coreutils` then `export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/lib" CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/include"` before building node native modules.

liam: i had homebrew in /usr/local which was x86; switched to /opt/homebrew and reinstalled packages. did `asdf plugin-add nodejs` and `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0` but after that `node -v` works, `npm -v` is missing.

jess: asdf nodejs plugin relies on the nodejs packaging to include npm; sometimes the plugin needs `bash` hooks. run `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring` if you see gpg warnings, then reinstall the version. also `asdf reshim` after install. if npm still missing, check `~/.asdf/installs/nodejs/18.16.0/bin` for npm and ensure your PATH has `~/.asdf/shims` before other node managers.

liam: ran the import keyring step and reshim, npm reappeared, thanks. quick chezmoi question: my dotfiles syncs `~/.zshrc` but my terminal is launching non-login zsh and asdf init isn't executed. where to put the eval so both login and non-login shells get it?

jess: put the `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"` and `source $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh` in `~/.zprofile` and `~/.zshrc` for zsh so login and interactive shells are covered. chezmoi can template both files; add it to the shared include. after changing, `exec zsh` to reload.

liam: one last small thing: devcontainer can't access my OP_SESSION token. i `op signin` on host and it prints a token, but it doesn't reach container. best pattern?

devex-bot: pattern: use `op signin --raw > ~/.op_token && docker run -v ~/.op_token:/tmp/op_token -e OP_SESSION_my=$(cat ~/.op_token) ...` or for devcontainer add a `postStartCommand` that reads a mounted token file into the container env. See https://intranet.redwood/dev-setup for examples.

liam: perfect, added the env mount in devcontainer.json and direnv now sees OP_SESSION. thanks for the quick help :raised_hands: ill update the chezmoi template to include asdf init so new hires don't hit this.

jess: great idea. ping #devex if you want us to PR the onboarding repo. :+1:
